newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK MARKET SHOWS INTEREST FOR EQUITY-LINKED BOND.
newsitem.headline: GREEK MARKET SHOWS INTEREST FOR EQUITY-LINKED BOND.

text.p: Subscriptions for National Mortgage Bank's one-year 3.0 percent equity-linked note based on a basket of six blue chip stocks are under way and the market is showing interest in the new product, sources at the issuer told Reuters.
Subscriptions which end February 11 are done through National Mortgage' branch network, NIBID , Societe Generale, Sigma Securities and National Securities.
"There is interest in the market for the equity-linked note, both retail and institutional," sources said.
The minimum subscription is one million drachmas. SBC Warburg and ING Barings Financial Products will place it abroad as well.

Along with the 3.0 percent coupon -- the capital guarantee feature of the instrument -- investors may benefit by the stock basket's upside potential as they will reap 50 percent of its return with no cap.
The note offers an innovative lock-in facility for predetermined returns. Investors have the option upon purchase to pick among four lock-in thresholds: open (no cap), 15, 20, and 25 percent.

The stock basket includes the following large caps: OTE, Hellenic Bottling , Alpha Credit Bank, National Bank , Titan Cement and National Mortgage Bank . --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
